mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI engine typically ranges from £1,200 for a used unit to £3,800-£6,000 for a fully rebuilt EA288 engine (supply-only).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing engine in an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Owners of the Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI should watch for persistent engine management lights, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power or limp mode.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most owners, it is financially viable. The Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI retains strong residual values, typically ranging from £8,000 to £35,000 depending on the generation and condition.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit engine replacement for an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI typically takes 2 to 3 working days.

mainEntity.name: Will any 2.0 TDI engine fit my Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must ensure the replacement engine matches your specific engine code (e.g., CAGB, CNHA, or DEJA) and is configured for your drivetrain (FWD or Quattro).

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI badge has been the backbone of the Audi A6 range, evolving from the C6 generation's pioneering common-rail diesels through the C7's refined EA189/EA288 units, to the C8's highly efficient mild-hybrid 35 TDI and 40 TDI variants.

milestones.description: CAGB, 2.0L TDI, 136-170hp. Introduced with the C6 generation, marking the transition to common-rail diesel technology for improved refinement and efficiency.
CAHA / CGLB, 2.0L TDI, 170hp. Launched with the C7 generation, featuring EA189 architecture with enhanced fuel economy and lower emissions.
CNHA, 2.0L TDI, 190hp. Introduced with the C7 facelift, utilising EA288 architecture to meet Euro 6 standards, commonly badged as 40 TDI.
DEJA / DEJB, 2.0L TDI Mild Hybrid, 150-204hp. Launched with the C8 generation, featuring a 12V mild-hybrid system for improved thermal efficiency, badged as 35 TDI and 40 TDI.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks & DPF Clogging - Why the Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI (CNHA/DEJA) Triggers Warning Lights
problems.affectedModels: Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI (CNHA, DEJA, DEJB, 2015-present)
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler is susceptible to internal micro-cracks, while frequent short urban journeys prevent the DPF from completing active regeneration, leading to ash buildup and increased backpressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty EGR cooler or professional DPF cleaning.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the core engine block and turbo are healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of reconditioned/rebuilt EA288 2.0 TDI, upgraded components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if multiple emissions components fail alongside high-mileage wear.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2018 Audi A6 40 TDI is valued at approximately £8,000-£18,000, while 2018+ C8 35/40 TDI models sit around £18,000-£35,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. For vehicles worth £8,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt replacement comfortably justifies the premium via warranty and reliability, keeping the repair cost well within the vehicle's retained value.
problems.recommendation: For isolated EGR or DPF faults on a well-maintained Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI, targeted component repair is the most cost-effective route. However, if the vehicle has exceeded 150k miles and exhibits concurrent issues, a reconditioned engine replacement offers superior long-term value and peace of mind.

problems.group: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear & Oil Pump Drive Issues
problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear & Oil Pump Drive Issues - High-Mileage Stress on the Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI (CAGB/CAHA)
problems.rootCause: Early common-rail 2.0 TDI units can experience timing chain stretch or tensioner wear, while some C7 variants are prone to oil pump drive gear wear, leading to catastrophic oil starvation if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Timing chain inspection and tensioner replacement.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable only if caught early, before structural damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt EA189 2.0 TDI, upgraded components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if oil starvation or chain jump has already occurred.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2004-2015 Audi A6 2.0 TDI is valued at approximately £3,000-£12,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. For sub-£5,000 examples, a high-quality used replacement may be more financially viable than a full rebuild, though a reconditioned unit remains the safest long-term investment if you plan to keep the car.
problems.recommendation: Preventative timing chain inspection at 80k miles is the best defence. If oil pump drive failure or chain jump has already occurred, replacing the entire unit with a rebuilt engine is safer than attempting standalone repairs, which risk recurring contamination or failure.

items.question: What are the signs of a failing engine in an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?
items.answer: Owners of the Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI should watch for persistent engine management lights, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power or limp mode.
keyPoints: Unusual rattling sounds from the engine bay on cold starts (timing chain).
Frequent AdBlue or DPF warning messages that do not clear after regeneration.
Unexplained coolant loss, which may indicate an EGR cooler leak.
items.cta: -> Get a diagnostic quote for your Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?
items.answer: Yes, for most owners, it is financially viable. The Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI retains strong residual values, typically ranging from £8,000 to £35,000 depending on the generation and condition.
keyPoints: A rebuilt engine is a sensible investment for a C8 (2018+) model.
For older C7 (2011-2018) models, a high-quality reconditioned unit offers excellent value if you plan to keep the car for 2+ years.
Always compare the replacement cost against the vehicle's current market value before proceeding.
items.cta: -> Check if your Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI is worth repairing

items.question: How long does an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI engine replacement take?
items.answer: A professional supply and fit engine replacement for an Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI typically takes 2 to 3 working days.
keyPoints: Day 1: Vehicle intake, draining of fluids, and careful removal of the faulty engine.
Day 2: Installation of the replacement engine, reconnection of the drivetrain, and refilling of fluids.
Day 3: ECU coding, software updates, and comprehensive road testing to ensure all systems are functioning correctly.
items.cta: -> Book your Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI supply & fit service

items.question: Will any 2.0 TDI engine fit my Audi A6 2.0 TDI / 35-40 TDI?
items.answer: No, you must ensure the replacement engine matches your specific engine code (e.g., CAGB, CNHA, or DEJA) and is configured for your drivetrain (FWD or Quattro).
keyPoints: Non-Quattro engines lack the necessary rear differential drive components and mounting points.
Using an incorrect engine code can result in ECU incompatibility, DPF/AdBlue system errors, and failed MOT emissions tests.
Entering your registration on EnginesMarket guarantees the quote is matched to your exact DVLA-registered engine specification.
